question: What claim about the uniqueness of this knowledge is at stake in denying that anything equal to it will exist again?
premises: Knowledge equal to this exists by comparison.
Such knowledge will not exist again.
A second negation reinforces its non-recurrence.
inference: No knowledge equal to this will arise again; it is presented as unique.
uncertainties: The scope of 'again' is not specified within this verse alone.
plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this; there will not be again, nor will there be.
